question: What is the main purpose of giving Oral Rehydration Therapy (ORT)?

options.A: To replace lost fluids and electrolytes
options.B: To provide daily nutritional caloric requirements
options.C: To stop the underlying infection causing diarrhea
options.D: To reduce the frequency of bowel movements

explanation: ORT doesn't stop the infection or the stooling right away. Its primary job is to put back the water and essential mineral salts that are washed out during vomiting and diarrhea.

question: Why is it so important to start ORT early when a patient has acute diarrhea?

options.A: It stimulates the appetite for solid foods
options.B: It immediately kills the bacteria in the gut
options.C: It coats the intestinal lining to prevent pain
options.D: It prevents rapid progression to hypovolemic shock

explanation: Catching fluid loss early stops the body's fluid levels from dropping to dangerously low levels that can lead to shock and organ failure.

question: Which substance must be present in a rehydration solution to help activate the SGLT1 transporter in the gut?
explanation: Think of glucose as a helpful partner! It teams up with sodium to attach to the SGLT1 transporter, which helps pull both molecules into the intestinal cells.

question: How does water move from inside the gut into the bloodstream during oral rehydration?

options.A: It follows sodium and glucose passively via osmosis
options.B: It is pumped across by high-pressure gradients
options.C: It travels through separate channels unaffected by solutes
options.D: It is pushed across by active muscular contractions

explanation: Water loves to follow where solutes go! When sodium and glucose are absorbed into the gut cells, water naturally follows them to keep the balance right.

question: Why do modern ORS packets use trisodium citrate instead of bicarbonate?

options.A: It gives the solution a sweeter taste for children
options.B: It speeds up the digestion of complex fats
options.C: It directly kills the parasites living in the gut
options.D: It makes the dry powder more stable during storage

explanation: Citrate handles hot, humid weather much better than bicarbonate, which means the ORS packets last longer without breaking down in our climate.

question: What is the main reason potassium chloride is included in standard ORS?

options.A: To provide energy for cellular repair processes
options.B: To increase the speed at which the fluid empties the stomach
options.C: To prevent dangerous heart rhythm changes from mineral loss
options.D: To thicken the solution so it stays in the gut longer

explanation: Frequent diarrhea drains the body's potassium levels. Replacing it is vital to prevent muscle weakness and serious heart issues.

question: What happens if a standard ORS packet is mixed with way too little water?

options.A: It tastes better and is easier for babies to swallow
options.B: It creates a hypertonic solution that worsens dehydration
options.C: It neutralizes stomach acid more rapidly
options.D: It becomes more effective at curing the infection

explanation: If there's too little water, the mixture becomes too salty and concentrated, actually pulling more water out of the body's tissues into the gut!

question: A mother says she mixed her child's ORS packet into half a liter of water instead of a full liter. What should you do?

options.A: Advise her to add extra sugar to balance out the high salt content
options.B: Instruct her to add another half-liter of water to the existing mixture and stir well
options.C: Allow her to feed the concentrated solution since it will work faster anyway
options.D: Discard the solution and help her mix a fresh batch correctly with one full liter of water

explanation: Guessing water amounts can throw off body chemistry. It is always safest to throw out the wrong mix and prepare a fresh, accurately measured batch.

question: Which sign is a key indicator of severe dehydration in a young child?

options.D: Eager drinking when offered a cup

explanation: When the body loses too much fluid and blood volume drops, the brain suffers, making the child very drowsy, limp, or unresponsive.

question: Why does a skin pinch test help nurses check a patient's hydration level?

options.A: Electrolyte imbalances cause immediate muscle contractions under the skin
options.B: Lack of blood flow makes the skin permanently thick and rigid
options.C: Dehydrated skin loses elasticity because interstitial fluid is depleted
options.D: Fever causes the skin cells to lock together tightly

explanation: When the fluid between skin cells dries up, the skin loses its natural stretchiness and takes longer to bounce back flat after pinching.

question: Which patient condition means Oral Rehydration Therapy is unsafe, requiring IV fluids instead?

options.A: Mild watery diarrhea with normal skin turgor
options.B: Profound hypovolemic shock with altered consciousness

explanation: If a patient is in shock or unconscious, they cannot swallow safely. They need quick intravenous fluids to restore their blood pressure.

question: What is an early sign of fluid overload to watch out for during rehydration therapy?

options.A: Rapid disappearance of skin pinch elasticity
options.B: Puffy eyelids and swelling around the eyes
options.C: Extreme thirst and dry cracked lips

explanation: Puffy eyes (periorbital edema) are a classic early warning that extra fluid and sodium are starting to build up in the body's tissues.

question: What feeding advice should a nurse give to a mother whose baby has acute diarrhea?

options.A: Stop all milk feeds for at least 48 hours to rest the gut
options.B: Withhold all food until the diarrhea stops completely
options.C: Replace breastmilk with plain water and sugar
options.D: Continue breastfeeding frequently throughout the illness

explanation: Never starve the gut! Breastfeeding gives the baby essential comfort, immune support, and nutrients to help them recover faster.

question: Why should we teach caregivers how to spot danger signs when managing diarrhea at home?

options.A: So they can seek professional medical help before complications become life-threatening
options.B: So they can safely administer intravenous fluids at home
options.C: To eliminate the need for any further follow-up visits
options.D: To prevent family members from catching the same infection

explanation: Spotting warning signs early—like extreme drowsiness or blood in the stool—helps parents rush the child to the clinic before things turn critical.
